case_title: SUBRAMANI @ JEEVA @ KULLAJEEVA v. S.H.O., ODIYANSALAI
evidence_type: Eyewitness, medical, recovery, test identification parade
high_court_outcome: Acquittal of six accused reversed, appellant convicted under s.304 (Part II) and sentenced to 3 years R.I.
offence_finally_established: Culpable homicide not amounting to murder
neutral_facts: The accused and the victim were at a restaurant where they ordered food and drinks. A dispute arose, leading to a confrontation. The accused broke a bottle and stabbed the victim on his neck. The victim and the victim's brother were injured during the incident. The victim was taken to the hospital and declared dead upon arrival. The accused were arrested and subjected to a test identification parade. The prosecution relied on eyewitness accounts, medical evidence, and the identification parade to establish the accused's involvement. The trial court acquitted all accused, but the High Court overturned the acquittal of the appellant, finding the incident to be the result of a sudden quarrel and thus falling under Exception 4 to Section 300 of the IPC.
